## MODULE 1 - TREND RESEARCH

Sources: Google Trends, Google News, YouTube, Reddit, GitHub Trending,
Product Hunt, OpenAI blog, Anthropic blog, Google AI blog (all via Tavily).

Ranks candidates by Virality / Search Interest / Novelty / Educational
Value / Long-term Search Potential. Selects exactly ONE topic.

## RELIABILITY NOTE

Modules 1-2 used to run Tavily as an AI-tool inside an autonomous agent
(ReAct loop). With small local Ollama models that loop was unreliable -
it repeatedly hit 'Max iterations reached' instead of answering, even
after raising maxIterations and tuning the prompt. Redesigned to be
DETERMINISTIC instead: a Code node builds the query, a plain HTTP Request
node calls the Tavily REST API directly (no agent, no tool, no loop),
then a tool-free LLM call (same pattern already proven reliable for the
Script/Storyboard/Visual Director/SEO steps) synthesizes the JSON.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: $json.trendQuery, topic: 'news', search_depth: 'advanced', days: 3, max_results: 10, include_answer: false }) }}

parameters.content:
## MODULE 2 - DEEP RESEARCH

Collects facts, stats, official docs and real announcements for the
selected topic. Every fact must carry a source URL. No invented info.
Fails the run if fewer than 3 sourced facts are found. Same deterministic
search-then-synthesize pattern as Module 1 (no agent/tool loop).

parameters.jsCode:
const query = 'Facts, statistics, official announcements, documentation and best practices about: ' + $json.topic + '. Context: ' + $json.whyNow;
return [{ json: { ...$json, deepQuery: query } }];

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: $json.deepQuery, search_depth: 'advanced', max_results: 10, include_answer: false }) }}

parameters.content:
## MODULE 3 - SCRIPT WRITER

Hook / Problem / Explanation / Real Example / Key Takeaway / CTA.
Max 170 words. Conversational Vietnamese. No repeated ideas.
Validated for word count + required structure before continuing.

## MODULE 4 - STORYBOARD

Splits the script into 5-8 dynamic scenes (45-70s total). Each scene:
duration, narration, subtitle, visual_description, camera_motion,
transition, emotion, text_overlay, animation_suggestion.

## MODULE 5 - VISUAL DIRECTION (most important)

Runs once per scene (after Normalize Storyboard splits into items).
No Sora / AI video generation - this is a REAL PHOTO slideshow format.
Produces two search queries per scene: event_query (specific real-world
photo of the actual event/company/person, for Tavily image search) and
stock_query (generic English description, Pexels fallback).

## LOOP OVER SCENES

Runs modules 6 (Voice), 7-partial (subtitle cue timing) and 8-partial
(real photo per scene via Tavily image search, Pexels stock-photo
fallback) once per scene. Final assembly (Ken Burns zoom + subtitle burn
+ ffmpeg edit) happens once after the loop completes.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: $json.scene.eventQuery, search_depth: 'basic', include_images: true, include_image_descriptions: false, max_results: 3 }) }}

parameters.fileName: ={{ $('Build Scene Subtitle Cues').first().json.scenesDir }}/scene_{{ String($('Build Scene Subtitle Cues').first().json.scene.sceneId).padStart(2,'0') }}_image.jpg

parameters.content:
## MODULE 7 (assembly) - SUBTITLES
## MODULE 8 (assembly) - VIDEO EDITING

Runs once, after the scene loop finishes (done branch, index 0).
Builds a karaoke-style .ass subtitle file (MrBeast-style keyword pop),
then an ffmpeg script: each scene image gets scale+crop to fill 1080x1920
plus a Ken Burns zoompan (per the storyboard's camera_motion), scenes are
joined with xfade transitions, bgm+sfx mixed with sidechain ducking,
loudnorm, subtitle burn-in.

## MODULE 9 - SEO

Title, description, keywords, hashtags + platform-specific captions.
Optimized for search/CTR - explicitly NOT clickbait.

## MODULE 10 - PUBLISHING

Uploads final_video.mp4 to YouTube (native node) and publishes to
TikTok (Content Posting API) + Facebook (Graph API Reels flow) via
HTTP Request. TikTok/Facebook calls require an approved developer app;
see PREMIUM_WORKFLOW.md for the exact onboarding steps.
